findings.finding: The mechanism has no traffic or timing precondition. A ModelId only appears in `list-metrics` after Bedrock has received at least one invocation for it and the datapoint has had time to show up. The plan runs the check as soon as the operator has applied terraform and redeployed. It then treats a missing 5.5 id as a mismatch to report as a bug. Right after a redeploy, a slot that hasn't been called yet is indistinguishable from a misspelled key.
findings.location: Approach (run timing and the 'If a 5.5 id is missing ... file a bug' branch); Acceptance Criteria line
scenarios: The verifier runs list-metrics minutes after the redeploy, before any frontier-class review has happened. The opus-5-5 series is missing and a false bug gets filed against correct alarm dimensions.
The haiku slot gets a call shortly before the check but its datapoint hasn't shown up in list-metrics yet. The check reports it as missing.
All three ids happen to appear. The check passes, but it was never clear that the absence path couldn't tell 'never called' from 'wrong key'.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, add a precondition before running list-metrics. Read the review bot's REBAR_USAGE_LOG (/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot/usage.jsonl) read-only through the existing SSM path. Confirm it has at least one successful Bedrock call for each of the bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-{opus,sonnet,haiku}-5-5 ids after the redeploy timestamp. Then wait a settling delay of roughly 15 minutes before running list-metrics. Treat an id with no logged call as 'not yet exercised': re-run later instead of filing a bug. File a bug only when the id was called but no matching ModelId series is listed, or the listed series is spelled differently. Extend the AC so it also records the timestamp of the most recent usage-log call for each id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before running `list-metrics`, confirm that each of the three 5.5 ids has been invoked since the redeploy and that at least 15 minutes have passed. Record an id with no invocations as 'inconclusive / not yet invoked', not as a mismatch to file a bug for.
evidence: Plan: "After the upgrade change has merged and the operator has applied the terraform and redeployed the production server, run the read-only `aws cloudwatch list-metrics ...`"
Plan: "If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series, or spelled differently, file a bug"

AWS CLI reference (docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudwatch/list-metrics.html, retrieved): "ListMetrics doesn't return information about metrics if those metrics haven't reported data in the past two weeks."
AWS SDK docs (pkg.go.dev/github.com/jechase/aws-sdk-go/service/cloudwatch, retrieved): "It can take up to fifteen minutes for a new metric to appear in calls to the ListMetrics action."
The plan has no step that gets each of the three slots invoked, or confirms they were, before the check runs.
findings.finding: The plan assumes `aws cloudwatch list-metrics` will list a ModelId series for each 5.5 profile once the terraform is applied and the server redeployed. ListMetrics only returns series that have reported data in the past two weeks, and a new series can take up to 15 minutes to appear. Bedrock creates a ModelId series only when that id is actually invoked. If any of the three slots (e.g. haiku/trivial) hasn't been called since the redeploy, its id will be missing from the output. Under the plan as written, that files a false bug, and the per-id match result in the AC can't distinguish 'wrong name' from 'not invoked yet'.
findings.location: Approach (list-metrics step and 'If a 5.5 id is missing ... file a bug'); Acceptance Criteria line 1
scenarios: The check runs soon after the redeploy, before any trivial-class review has used haiku. `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5` is absent, so a bug is filed even though the id may be correct.
The check runs within 15 minutes of the first opus invocation. The series doesn't show up yet, and the check reports a false mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Approach step: before running list-metrics, confirm (e.g. from the bot's usage/invocation logs) that each of opus, sonnet and haiku 5.5 has been called at least once since the redeploy, then wait at least 15 minutes. File the `discovered_from` bug only when an id that was invoked is still missing or spelled differently. Record ids with no invocations as inconclusive in the ticket comment, and re-run once traffic has reached them.

Evidence class: Partially-verified. The `aws cloudwatch` CLI family is used in this repo (get-metric-statistics, describe-alarms), but the `list-metrics` subcommand and its rule that series appear only once data exists were not observed via --help in this environment.
findings.finding: The plan reads 'a 5.5 id is missing from the published series' as a dimension mismatch to file as a bug. But `list-metrics` only returns a series after Bedrock has published at least one datapoint for it, and the plan has no step confirming that each of the three slots (frontier/opus, standard/sonnet, trivial/haiku) was invoked after the redeploy. A missing series could just mean no traffic yet, so the check can't tell 'never called' from 'published under a different ModelId'.

findings.finding: The probe can report a false 'missing' result. `list-metrics` only returns a ModelId series after Bedrock has emitted at least one datapoint for it. The plan runs the command right after the redeploy but never requires that the bot has invoked each of the opus, sonnet and haiku 5.5 profiles first. A model the bot rarely uses (e.g. opus) may not appear yet, and the executor would then file a spurious bug.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require evidence that each of the three 5.5 models has been invoked after the redeploy before running list-metrics, and treat 'absent with no confirmed invocation' as inconclusive (re-check), not as a bug.

Absence: no requirement that each of opus/sonnet/haiku 5.5 has served at least one invocation before the check.
findings.finding: `list-metrics` returns only series that have received data points (within roughly the last two weeks). Right after the redeploy, a 5.5 model that has not yet been invoked has no published series at all. The plan's rule ('If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series ... file a bug') would then misreport 'no traffic yet' as a dimension mismatch. A rarely used model such as haiku would be especially likely to trip this. The plan sets no precondition that each of the three models has actually been invoked post-redeploy, so 'missing' is not a faithful proof of a misspelled dimension.
findings.location: Approach — 'run the read-only `aws cloudwatch list-metrics` ... If a 5.5 id is missing from the published series ... file a bug'
scenarios: The check runs minutes after redeploy; haiku-5-5 has not been called, so its series is absent and a spurious bug is filed.
A genuinely missing series is dismissed as 'no traffic yet' because the plan gives no way to tell the two cases apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition step: confirm at least one post-redeploy invocation per 5.5 model, by bot logs or by a deliberate read-only review run that exercises each tier. Only then run list-metrics. Optionally also run `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics` with each alarm's exact ModelId dimension and confirm non-empty datapoints.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Retitle the plan to describe the verification (e.g. 'Verify Bedrock publishes metrics under the 5.5 alarm ModelId dimensions') rather than the upgrade change it checks.
evidence: Title: 'Point deploy model defaults and Bedrock alarms at the 5.5 inference profiles'
Scope: 'None: this verification changes no repository file.'
Context: 'The model-upgrade task `beaten-natural-grouse` moves the production compose defaults ... and the Bedrock CloudWatch alarm dimensions'
findings.finding: The title promises a change ('Point deploy model defaults and Bedrock alarms at the 5.5 inference profiles'). The body explicitly does no such work: it is a post-merge verification of task `beaten-natural-grouse`'s change and 'changes no repository file'. The headline intent and the body's deliverable disagree.
scenarios: An implementer reading the title edits docker-compose.yml / monitoring_eb6e.tf, duplicating or conflicting with beaten-natural-grouse.
A reviewer closes this ticket believing the cutover itself was delivered here.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle to 'Verify published AWS/Bedrock ModelId series match the 5.5 alarm dimensions after beaten-natural-grouse deploys'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare a depends_on edge to `beaten-natural-grouse`, and add a read-only precheck confirming the applied alarms and the deployed defaults carry the 5.5 ids; if either is absent, stop and comment that the prerequisites are not met.
evidence: "After the upgrade change has merged and the operator has applied the terraform and redeployed the production server"
ABSENCE: no command confirms the applied alarm dimensions or the deployed model defaults; no depends_on edge is named.
findings.finding: The prerequisite state (upgrade merged, terraform applied, server redeployed) is assumed, not verified. No dependency edge on `beaten-natural-grouse` is declared. If the apply or redeploy has not happened, the executor will compare live metrics against alarms or model defaults that do not yet exist, and nothing tells it to stop.
scenarios: The operator has merged the change but not yet run terraform apply. The live alarms still name the old ids, and the check compares the wrong thing.
The session starts before the operator steps, and the executor has no stated rule to block or wait.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precheck: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --profile frontier --region us-east-1 --query 'MetricAlarms[].{n:AlarmName,d:Dimensions}' --output json` must show the three 5.5 ModelId values, and the deployed server's model env must match compose lines 97-99. Record both in the ticket comment. If either fails, block the task rather than proceed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the alarm-dimension values compared are read from the live alarms via `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` (read-only), not only from the repo terraform file.
evidence: "compare each listed `ModelId` with the three alarm dimensions character for character"
Context cites `infra/terraform/monitoring_eb6e.tf:80-135` as where the dimensions are defined.
findings.finding: The plan does not say where the 'three alarm dimensions' come from: the repo file `monitoring_eb6e.tf` or the live applied alarms. The point of the check is what CloudWatch actually keys on, so the live alarm values are the authoritative side of the comparison. The plan leaves this choice to the executor.
scenarios: The repo matches but the applied state differs (partial apply or drift). The executor compares against the repo and reports a match that the live alarms do not have.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comparison sentence to: compare each listed ModelId with the ModelId dimension values returned by `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` for the Bedrock alarms defined in monitoring_eb6e.tf:80-135.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State as a default that us-east-1 is both the Bedrock invocation region of the production bot and the provider region of monitoring_eb6e.tf, and record that confirmation in the ticket comment.
evidence: "--profile frontier --region us-east-1"
ABSENCE: no statement linking us-east-1 to the bot's AWS region or the terraform provider region for monitoring_eb6e.tf.
findings.finding: The plan hardcodes `--region us-east-1` without saying it is the region where the bot's Bedrock client and the alarms live. Bedrock emits cross-region inference-profile metrics in the source (calling) region. If production calls Bedrock from another region, the query returns nothing and wrongly signals 'missing'.
scenarios: The bot runs with AWS_REGION=us-west-2. Its metrics land there, us-east-1 shows no 5.5 series, and a spurious bug is filed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extract the published ModelId values with `--query 'Metrics[].Dimensions[?Name==`ModelId`].Value[]' --output json` and assert exact membership of each alarm id (e.g. with `jq -e 'index("<id>")'`), recording each assertion's result.
evidence: "compare each listed `ModelId` with the three alarm dimensions character for character"
ABSENCE: no --query/jq extraction or exact-equality assertion is specified.
findings.finding: The per-id match is judged by a person reading the raw list-metrics output (taxonomy item 6: prose rather than structured assertion). Because the risk being guarded against is a near-identical spelling difference, the comparison should be a mechanical exact-string check on structured JSON.
scenarios: An id that differs only in a version suffix (e.g. a `-v1:0` tail) is misread as a match on visual inspection.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace AWS/Bedrock --metric-name Invocations --profile frontier --region us-east-1 --query 'Metrics[].Dimensions[?Name==`ModelId`].Value[]' --output json > published.json`. Then, for each alarm id, run `jq -e --arg id "$ID" 'index($id) != null' published.json` and record the exit code per id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Read the alarm dimensions from the deployed alarms (read-only `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms` in the alarms' region) and record them alongside list-metrics, stating that us-east-1 is the bot's invocation and alarm region.
evidence: 'compare each listed `ModelId` with the three alarm dimensions character for character'
'--profile frontier --region us-east-1'
'applying terraform and redeploying are operator steps, not part of this task'
findings.finding: The plan compares listed ModelIds 'with the three alarm dimensions' without saying where those values are read from. The repo file `monitoring_eb6e.tf` and the deployed alarms can differ, for example after a partial apply or drift. The plan treats the operator's terraform apply as a precondition but does not verify it. Only the deployed alarm's dimension decides whether paging works. The region is also hardcoded to us-east-1 without stating that this is the region where the bot invokes Bedrock and where the alarms live.
findings.location: Approach — 'compare each listed `ModelId` with the three alarm dimensions character for character'
scenarios: The operator's apply partially failed: the repo shows 5.5 dimensions, the deployed alarms still use old ids, and the check passes against the repo text.
The bot invokes from another region where its metrics and alarms live; us-east-1 list-metrics shows nothing and a spurious bug is filed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --profile frontier --region us-east-1` filtered to the Bedrock alarms. Record each alarm's `ModelId` dimension in the ticket comment and use those values, not the .tf text, as the comparison side.
